entry.title: Blueprints: The Edge's U2 Guitar Sound

media:group.media:title: Blueprints: The Edge's U2 Guitar Sound
media:group.media:description:
You don't need a stadium rack to sound like the Edge. PG Contributor ⁨@TomButwin⁩ breaks U2's guitarist down to the pillars of his sound: a cranked Vox, dual delays running into the amp's front end, a transparent overdrive, a Gibson Explorer, and a right hand that doesn't miss. Instead of trying to clone The Edge's rig, which changes constantly and is far bigger than most of us will ever run, he builds the foundation.
The Vox AC15 Hand-Wired does most of the work, set to the top boost channel. The Eventide H9 Harmonizer Gen 2 handles both delays and runs into the amp's front end, the way the Edge does it. A Mr. Black Deuce Coupe drives the amp without coloring the tone, and it cleans up off the guitar's volume knob. Then Tom gets to the '70s Explorer, (thanks @sweetwater!) the accuracy the Edge's parts demand from your picking hand, and a pick trick you'll want to steal.

entry.title: P-90, Filter'Tron, And Specialty Classics | Pickups Demystified Ep. 3

media:group.media:title: P-90, Filter'Tron, And Specialty Classics | Pickups Demystified Ep. 3
media:group.media:description:
The humbucker-versus-single-coil debate has a blind spot. Technically, a P-90 is a single coil and a Filter'Tron is a humbucker, so both get filed away with the usual suspects. Plug one in and you'll hear why that shortcut doesn't hold up.
In the final episode of Pickups Demystified, Tom Butwin digs into the specialty pickups that share a family tree with the two big categories but took their own path. The P-90 uses a wider coil and bar magnets for a grittier midrange than any Strat-style single coil. The Filter'Tron cancels hum like a PAF, but its narrow bobbins and thicker magnet give it a brighter, tighter voice. Tom walks through the history behind each design and highlights modern takes, including a few that drop straight into a humbucker route.
Then come the outliers. The Charlie Christian blade pickup dates back to the 1930s and helped turn the electric guitar into a lead instrument. The wide-range humbucker was Fender's oversized answer to Gibson in the early seventies, designed by Seth Lover, the same engineer behind the PAF.
If your tone lives somewhere the usual two can't reach, start here.

entry.title: Gibson Changed How Its Acoustic Guitars Sound Plugged In

media:group.media:title: Gibson Changed How Its Acoustic Guitars Sound Plugged In
media:group.media:description:
